newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy in favorable business shape -- Minn Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy in favorable business shape -- Minn Fed.

text.p: The president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, Gary Stern, said the U.S. economy is in good shape and well-positioned for another year of growth.
"We find ourselves in favorable business and financial circumstances which have every prospect of continuing," Stern told an audience here during a Minneapolis Fed community conference.
"The economy is remarkably well-positioned for another year of growth," the Minneapolis Fed chief added.

Stern said U.S. inflation remains under control even though unemployment is perceived to be dropping. He said the economy was characterized by "modest inflation, advancing equity prices and falling unemployment."
Asked about whether he saw any possible threats that may eventually haunt the U.S. economy in the near future, Stern said "I wouldn't care to cite any."
Stern was the only member of the Federal Open Market Committee to vote against the maintenance of a steady monetary policy in the latter half of last year.

The Fed kept rates steady until March 25 when it raised its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent during the last meeting of its policy-setting body. The minutes of that meeting will not be available until after the next FOMC gathering on May 20./
Stern is not scheduled to vote on FOMC policy actions in 1997 given the committee's rotation rules.
